name: masters-pods-cups/seal-a
refs: THE PAINTED LANGUAGE (one of our signed room paintings, project-owned): its matte painterly miniature rendering, soft occlusion, warm golden key light from the upper left and cosy palette. Take the treatment and the warmth only, none of its objects.
prompt: Paint ONE wax seal seen straight from above (perfectly front-on, a flat round disc facing us): a disc of deep wine-red sealing wax, its outer edge irregular and softly squashed outward like real poured wax, with small rounded bulges, clearly NOT a perfect circle and NOT a coin: no raised rim, no milled edge, no metal. In its middle, pressed into the wax, a simple, bold impressed mark: the plain upright silhouette of a seed pod (a rounded egg shape with a small round cap on top), deeply pressed so it reads by its shadow inside the impression and its lit lip. The mark is not a star, not a flower, not a sprout, not a leaf, not a letter. Key light from the upper left: the wax's raised lip catches a soft warm highlight at the upper left, the impression's upper-left inner wall is in shadow. Deep wine red (#7a1f2b), rich but low in gloss, never orange, never pink, never bright scarlet. The seal fills about 80 percent of the picture, centred. The seal lies alone on a perfectly FLAT, uniform, pure green background (#00B140) that fills the whole rest of the picture edge to edge: no gradient, no texture, no paper, no ribbon, no cast shadow on the background, no green reflected in the wax. Nothing else in the picture: no text, letters, numbers or symbols, no frame, no border. Matte, hand-painted miniature finish like our room paintings, low saturation, warm and calm; soft occlusion; no gloss, no chrome, no plastic, no photo-realism, no outlines.
